title: Business Central 29: How Many Fields Can a Table Really Have?

chapters.title: Introduction and context about field limits
Detect table approaching SQL column limit warning

Companion table behavior and iterative testing
Testing SQL limit and schema best practices

features.name: Detect table approaching SQL column limit warning
features.description: A compiler warning introduced in Business Central 29 that alerts AL developers when tables or table extensions containing many normal fields are approaching the SQL extensibility limit.
caveats: Does not mean the limit is absolute
Different data types affect the calculation

features.name: New table extension data model
features.description: Business Central 29 changed how table extension fields are stored - they are now stored in the same SQL server table as base table fields instead of in a separate companion table, improving database performance by approximately 30%.
caveats: Changes how field limits are calculated
Requires understanding of new storage model

features.name: 300 field warning threshold
features.description: The system generates a warning when a table with extensions reaches 300 combined fields total (293 user-defined fields plus 6-7 system platform fields), indicating developers should not add more fields to that table.
caveats: 300 is a warning threshold, not a hard limit
Different from SQL Server's 500 column maximum
Actual limit depends on data types and record size
Allows publishing with more than 300 fields
Warning threshold appears to vary based on field types used

features.name: Platform system fields
features.description: Business Central automatically adds 6 system fields to every table: system ID, system created at, system created by, system modified at, system modified by, and row version, which count toward the field limit.
caveats: These fields are mandatory and count toward limits
Not visible in standard table designer view

features.name: Record size byte limit
features.description: The maximum record size in bytes for each record is 8060 bytes at the SQL server level.
caveats: Applies to all fields combined in a table
Platform-defined fields count toward this limit
Actual field count limit depends on data types

features.name: Data type byte consumption
features.description: Different field data types consume different amounts of bytes: decimal takes 17 bytes while integer takes 4 bytes, affecting how many fields can fit in a table.
caveats: Text and code types vary based on length
